vision_features.image_context: Ground-level view of a field or garden bed showing dry, pale sandy-gray soil with scattered dry plant debris (dead stems and twigs). Multiple young seedling plants with broad green leaves are visible around the edges. The central focus is a single small seedling plant that appears severely affected, standing upright near the center of the frame. The plant organs visible include the stem and remnants of cotyledons/early leaves of the central plant, plus healthy-looking leaves of surrounding seedlings.
vision_features.abnormalities: Central plant stem: The stem of the central seedling is dark brown to nearly black in color from the soil level upward, appearing thin, dry, and shrunken compared to the healthy green stems of surrounding plants. The darkened stem tissue spans approximately 3–5 cm in length and is elongated, following the stem axis. The texture appears dry, shriveled, and constricted — notably narrowed at or just above the soil line, giving a pinched, thread-like appearance at that point. At the top of the darkened stem, there is a small, pale yellow-cream colored structure approximately 5–8 mm across that appears twisted or contorted, possibly the growing tip or cotyledon remnants in a deformed state. Just below this, there is a small piece of collapsed, papery, tan-to-light-brown tissue (approximately 10–15 mm) that is limp and flat, likely a collapsed early leaf or cotyledon. No green tissue is visible on the central plant. The overall plant is very small (total height approximately 4–6 cm above ground). The abnormality is confined entirely to the central plant; surrounding seedlings appear unaffected with normal green coloration.
vision_features.absences: 1. No powdery or fuzzy surface coating is visible on the affected stem or collapsed tissue. 2. No visible raised bumps, pustules, or tiny embedded dots on any part of the affected plant. 3. No yellowing of surrounding soil or plant tissue adjacent to the affected seedling. 4. No visible root tissue is exposed or showing discoloration above the soil surface.
vision_features.summary: The image shows a field of young seedlings in sandy soil, with one central seedling in severe distress. The central plant's stem is dark brown to black, dry, and markedly constricted at or near the soil line, with the remainder of the above-ground plant collapsed into papery, tan, lifeless tissue. The surrounding seedlings appear healthy and green by contrast, highlighting that the damage is localized to this single plant. The most striking feature is the extreme constriction and darkening of the stem at the soil level, combined with the complete collapse of all above-ground tissue, leaving only a pale, twisted remnant at the tip.
